unsupported_claims: Such methods (implicitly including the paper's method) often use global recomputation because new walks from a changed region can shift the shared embedding space and misalign vectors for unchanged nodes.

Walks started only in the changed region give a biased sample of co-occurrence statistics, so recomputation keeps embeddings consistent; this goes along with the premise that global recomputation is preferred.
rationale: The answer never corrects the false premise; the paper says small graph changes can be handled without global recomputation, by updating the model with new random walks from the changed region in sub-linear time. Instead it offers generic reasons why recomputation is preferable, which the evidence contradicts, so the core of the answer is unsupported.
